retain_for_fulltext.instructions: Should this citation be retained for full-text assessment in a systematic review of experimental animal models of depression? Use only the supplied title and abstract. Retain potentially eligible primary experimental research in living non-human animals that involves an in vivo experimental manipulation and investigates a depression model or depressive-like phenotype. Model-characterisation and treatment studies may be eligible; a separate treatment arm is not required. All animal species, ages and sexes are eligible. Exclude clearly identified reviews, editorials, letters, comments, case reports and conference- or seminar-only abstracts. Exclude human-only research, purely observational investigations without experimental manipulation, and studies confined to ex vivo, in vitro or in silico work. Mixed human/animal studies or studies with additional laboratory components remain potentially eligible when a qualifying in vivo animal investigation is present. Consider the authors' stated research aims, experimental manipulation and interpretation of the phenotype. Antidepressant administration alone does not establish a depression model. A behavioural test may support potential eligibility, but its presence alone does not conclusively establish the disease model. Retain ambiguous cases, including antidepressant-only behavioural studies when the depression-model component cannot be determined. Retain studies investigating a depression model or depressive-like phenotype alongside another psychiatric condition, including studies framed as bipolar disorder when a depression-related component is investigated. Do not exclude solely because the broader study is framed as another disorder. Exclude only when the supplied text clearly establishes that another condition is investigated without a depression-related component. Distinguish depressive-like phenotypes from unrelated uses of depression, such as respiratory depression. Do not require a particular behavioural test or an explicitly reported model-induction method when eligibility remains uncertain. Assess comparator and outcome eligibility at full-text screening; neither control-group nor outcome grounds may independently cause exclusion in this primary title-and-abstract classification. Missing or ambiguous reporting favours retention. Retain uncertain cases unless another primary screening criterion clearly establishes ineligibility.

criteria.true: Retain for full-text assessment, including potentially eligible studies and citations with uncertain eligibility.
criteria.false: Clearly ineligible on primary publication type, live-animal population, in vivo experimental manipulation or depression-model grounds.
